key_facts.answer: Moving a dog from Dubai to the USA needs a USDA-endorsed health certificate, a CDC Dog Import Form receipt, a microchip and rabies cover. The dog must be at least 6 months old on arrival and appear healthy at the port of entry. Because the UAE is a dog-rabies low-risk origin, the CDC form and the 6-month age rule are what catch people out, not a rabies titre test.

takeaways: Every dog needs a CDC Dog Import Form receipt — fill it out online before travel.
The dog must be at least 6 months old on arrival.
A microchip readable by a universal scanner is mandatory and must be recorded before the form.
The dog must appear healthy at entry.
Typical cost Dubai → USA: an estimate of roughly AED 13,800–22,000, typically about 4–12 weeks.

sections.heading: The short answer
paragraphs: To bring a dog into the USA from Dubai, the CDC requires that every dog has a CDC Dog Import Form receipt, is at least 6 months old, is microchipped (readable by a universal scanner), and appears healthy on arrival.

The UAE is treated as a dog-rabies low-risk origin, so a US rabies certificate isn't the hurdle — the CDC form and the 6-month age rule are what catch people out. Plan around them and the move is straightforward.

sections.heading: What the CDC requires
paragraphs: Since the CDC's updated dog-import rules, all dogs entering the USA must travel with a CDC Dog Import Form receipt, be at least six months old, be microchipped, and look healthy at the port of entry. Dogs from low-risk countries like the UAE don't need extra rabies documentation, but they still must meet every one of those baseline conditions.
There's no shortcut on the age rule: a puppy under six months simply cannot enter, however complete the rest of the paperwork is.

sections.heading: The order that keeps you compliant
bullets: Microchip first — it's the identity that ties every later document together.
Confirm the dog will be 6 months old on the travel date before booking anything.
Submit the CDC Dog Import Form in the window the CDC specifies before arrival and keep the receipt.
UAE export side — MOCCAE export permit and a fit-to-fly health certificate.

sections.heading: Your documents, in order
paragraphs: Working through the requirements already covered above in the order they need to happen:
bullets: 1. Microchip — implant a chip readable by a universal scanner first; it ties every later document together.
2. Confirm the 6-month age rule — check the dog will be at least 6 months old on the arrival date before booking.
3. Health certificate — a USDA-endorsed, fit-to-fly health certificate.
4. MOCCAE export permit — the UAE export-side permit.
5. CDC Dog Import Form — submit it in the window the CDC specifies before arrival and keep the receipt.
6. Booking — arrange the flight once the above are in hand.

story.lead: On the USA route, the trap usually isn't rabies — it's age and the form.
story.problem: A family wants to fly their 5-month-old puppy to the US with them next month.
story.mistake: They assume healthy-and-vaccinated is enough and don't check the age rule or the CDC form.
story.discovery: The puppy is under six months, so it can't enter — and no one submitted the CDC Dog Import Form.
story.result: The puppy stays in boarding until it's old enough, then flies separately — extra cost and a hard goodbye at the airport.
story.lesson: For the USA, check two things first: the dog's age on arrival and the CDC form. Everything else is routine.

faqs.q: Do I need a CDC Dog Import Form for a dog from Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. Every dog entering the USA must travel with a CDC Dog Import Form receipt, regardless of origin.

faqs.q: How old must my dog be?
faqs.a: At least six months on the date of arrival. This applies to all dogs entering the USA.

faqs.q: Does my dog need a rabies titre test for the USA?
faqs.a: No. The UAE is treated as a dog-rabies low-risk origin, so the focus is the CDC form, the age rule, microchip and overall health — not a titre test.

faqs.q: Which airline is best for pets leaving the UAE?
faqs.a: It depends on your dog's size and the season; in the summer heat embargo, options narrow. We match the route to your pet rather than a single carrier.

method.structure_logic: 2026 article anatomy: headline (curiosity/result) -> answer-first opening (the liftable answer in the first lines) -> key takeaways -> table of contents -> scannable H2/H3 -> a visual (data table or flow) -> original insight or a story -> FAQ -> official sources -> one help-first CTA. Why: web readers scan ~20-28% of words (Nielsen Norman Group), so the answer is front-loaded; a story is remembered where bare facts are forgotten; one page = one job + a single CTA converts. These choices recur across every source in our research (see SOURCING-METHOD.md).
method.geo_seo_rationale: What we believe helps. GEO (being cited by AI answer engines): answer-first self-contained chunks, cited statistics, official-source citations, consistent entities, FAQ schema -- and citation is decoupled from ranking (~66% of AI-Overview citations come from outside the top-20), so strong content can be cited even before it ranks. SEO: intent-matched title+H1, topical depth, internal links into the money page, visible freshness dates, structured data (Article/FAQ/Breadcrumb/LocalBusiness). HONEST CAVEAT: these are evidence-based best practices, NOT guaranteed results -- ranking also needs off-page authority/backlinks/indexing not built here, and GEO citation is plausible but unproven until measured with a live AI-citation test.
method.how_and_why_we_audit: Each page is scored by a 5-lens auditor -- Website, SEO, GEO, Lead-gen/Trust, Quality -- which together cover the 7-category QA (Helpful, Human, Original, Trustworthy, SEO, GEO, Conversion). Why this way: (1) page-type profiles judge a page against ITS job (a reassurance page is weighted differently from a money page); (2) every check carries an evidence tier (T1 sworn -> T6 practitioner) and a verified-vs-heuristic tag; (3) not-measurable checks are excluded, never zeroed (a coverage->confidence label); (4) risk caps catch keyword-stuffing, thin content, fake schema, no-CTA. The score is an on-page QUALITY PROXY, not a measured ranking/citation outcome.
method.what_we_are_sure_of: 100% sure = a fact screenshot-verified against its official source as of a date (see sourcing.verified_100pct) + that the method was applied. NOT sure = that it ranks or gets cited (unproven until the site is live, indexed and measured).
method.how_we_verify: Every factual/regulatory claim is verified against an OFFICIAL source only -- government bodies, recognised standards bodies (IATA), or the operator's own site (e.g. the airline). Never blogs, forums, competitors, or AI. Each verified claim is captured as a full-page SCREENSHOT and logged in a regulatory register with: source, URL, date verified, version, reviewer, and a re-verify-by date (because regulations change). Anything we could not confirm from an official source is HEDGED or flagged 'confirm with [authority]', never asserted (see sourcing.stated_but_unverified). Tooling: a Playwright screenshot verifier with an official-domain allowlist + the regulatory register. Facts are kept separate from advice ('the authority requires X' vs 'we recommend X'). AI never makes the final call -- a human reviews and signs off before publish.

sourcing.how_we_derived_this: Built from recurring patterns across our research corpus (SOURCING-METHOD.md): answer the fear not the keyword, front-load the answer, official sources only, a route-specific story, single help-first CTA into the money page.
